ecommerceApi.name: E-Commerce REST API
ecommerceApi.summary: A layered e-commerce backend with JWT authentication, role-based authorization, a product catalog and a cart — documented end to end in Swagger.
highlights: JWT authentication with Admin / User roles securing 10+ endpoints
Clean Architecture: Controller → Service → Repository
Product CRUD with pagination and search / filter by name and category
Cart module: add items, update quantities and remove — 3 dedicated endpoints
Swagger / OpenAPI docs with Bearer-token support
ecommerceApi.caseStudy: Controllers stay thin and hand each request to a service, which holds the business rules and reaches the data through repository interfaces. Entity Framework Core (Code First migrations) maps the domain to SQL Server, and admin-only operations sit behind role-based authorization. Swagger documents every endpoint and accepts a Bearer token, so the whole API can be explored without a frontend.

flow.title: Controllers
flow.detail: Routing, JWT auth and role policies

paymob.name: Paymob Payment Integration
paymob.summary: A complete card-payment flow on Paymob: payment sessions created on the server, signed webhooks, and a result page that can't be faked.
highlights: Payment sessions created on the server — API keys never reach the browser
HMAC-SHA512 verification of every webhook and redirect, compared in constant time
The webhook is the source of truth: a forged ?success=true URL shows “verification failed”
Duplicate deliveries are safe: results are keyed per order, and a late callback can't overwrite a successful payment
Two flows from one codebase: an embedded card iframe or Paymob Unified Checkout
paymob.caseStudy: Built with Next.js Route Handlers and strict TypeScript types for every Paymob payload. The checkout endpoint authenticates with Paymob, registers the order and issues a payment key from server-only modules, with request timeouts and typed errors. When Paymob calls the webhook, the handler rebuilds the 20 signed fields, computes HMAC-SHA512 and compares it in constant time before recording anything — and answers 500 on failure so Paymob retries. The checkout page polls a status endpoint fed only by verified results, so the customer always lands on the right success or failure screen.

lms.name: Learning Management System
lms.summary: A full-featured LMS built as the DEPI graduation project: courses, instructors, enrollments and three user roles on a clean three-layer architecture.
highlights: Three-layer architecture: Presentation, Business Logic (BLL) and Data Access (DAL)
ASP.NET Core Identity with Admin, Instructor and Student roles
Admin dashboard with statistics on courses, categories, instructors and enrollments
Course search and filtering, enrollment management and student profiles
Repository pattern, service layer and dependency injection throughout
lms.caseStudy: Built as a team for the Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative (DEPI). The MVC layer only renders views and calls services; the BLL owns the course and enrollment rules; the DAL wraps Entity Framework Core in repositories over SQL Server. Every layer is wired through ASP.NET Core's dependency injection, and ASP.NET Core Identity handles registration, sign-in and role-based authorization for all three roles.

churn.name: Customer Churn Prediction
churn.summary: A model that flags the customers most likely to cancel, so a retention team knows exactly who to call first.
highlights: 80.3% accuracy and 0.848 ROC-AUC on a held-out test set (baseline: 73.5%)
The riskiest 20% of customers contain 51% of all churners — about 2.5× better than random
Soft-voting ensemble of CatBoost, XGBoost and Logistic Regression
Five model families tuned with Optuna on 5-fold stratified cross-validation
A scoring CLI that outputs a churn probability and risk tier for each customer
churn.caseStudy: Trained on the public IBM Telco dataset (7,043 customers). A stratified 20% test set is locked away and used exactly once, at the end, so the reported numbers are an honest estimate. Feature engineering — service counts, average spend, a price-change signal — lives inside the scikit-learn pipeline, so nothing leaks between folds and the same code runs at prediction time. The saved pipeline scores new customers from a CSV and sorts them by risk.

samehKasem.name: Dr. Sameh Kasem
samehKasem.summary: An Arabic-first medical portal for a consultant in brain, nerve and spine surgery — designed to turn search traffic into booked consultations.
highlights: Custom appointment booking forms

Medical schema markup targets condition and procedure searches, while the clinic team manages reviews and procedures from a Supabase dashboard — no developer needed.

highlights: CMS dashboard to manage projects, photo galleries and articles — no developer needed
Portfolio filtered by sector, with its own page and photo gallery for every project
Blog with categories, reading time, related articles and one-tap sharing

Every public page is pre-rendered as static HTML with LocalBusiness structured data, an XML sitemap and Open Graph tags, so the studio's work loads fast and is easy for Google to understand.

About.title: One developer, accountable for your project from first call to launch
bio: I'm Mohamed Ali, a full-stack engineer working across the .NET and Next.js ecosystems. Twenty-plus websites in, I've learned that clients don't buy frameworks — they buy more bookings, more inquiries and less hassle.

So every site I ship is built mobile-first, set up properly for Google from day one, and comes with a dashboard simple enough to update without calling a developer. You work with one person who designs, builds, launches and supports it — and who answers on WhatsApp.

edit.q: Can I update the content myself?
edit.a: Yes. Every project includes a dashboard where you edit text, images, articles, reviews or products — no code and no developer needed.

own.a: Completely. The domain, hosting and source code are set up under your own accounts, so you're never locked in.

time.a: It depends on the size of the project and the features you need. After our first call you get a clear, agreed timeline together with the quote — and you follow the progress on a live preview link throughout.

cost.q: How much does a website cost?
cost.a: Pricing depends on the number of pages and features. After a short call you receive a clear written quote — no hidden costs.

google.q: Will my site show up on Google?
google.a: Every site ships with technical SEO done right: speed optimisation, structured data, sitemaps and Search Console setup. Rankings also depend on competition and content, and I'll tell you honestly what to expect.

after.a: You get support after launch for fixes and small adjustments, and I'm available for new features or ongoing maintenance whenever you need them.
